nodes.label: MQ-135 Gas Sensor Module
nodes.description: Product photograph of a purple breakout PCB carrying an MQ-135 metal-oxide semiconductor gas sensor. The dome-shaped stainless steel mesh cap covers the internal heater and SnO2 sensing element; the mesh acts as a flame arrestor and diffusion barrier. Board is silkscreened 'MQx' with a Sensor-brand wave logo.
nodes.rationale: The MQ-135 is chosen for air-quality/ammonia and CO2-equivalent gas sensing in a poultry/livestock or environmental monitoring rig because it is low cost, 5V-powered, and exposes both an analog concentration output and a comparator-thresholded digital alarm, letting a controller act on gas levels without ADC calibration if needed.

nodes.label: LM393 Dual Comparator (on-board threshold circuit)
nodes.description: SOIC-8 chip marked 'LM393 IDCAB29' mounted on the MQ-135 breakout. It compares the sensor's analog voltage against a reference set by the on-board trim potentiometer and drives the DO digital output plus its indicator LED.

nodes.label: Sensitivity Adjust Potentiometer
nodes.description: Blue/silver multi-turn trimmer silkscreened 'ADJUST' that sets the comparator reference voltage, i.e. the gas concentration threshold at which DO trips.
nodes.rationale: Provides field-tunable trip point so the same board can be calibrated to a target ammonia/CO2 threshold for the enclosure without changing firmware.

nodes.label: MQ-135 4-Pin Interface (5V, DO, AO, GND)
nodes.description: Four labelled header pads on the board edge: 5V, DO (digital comparator output), AO (raw analog sensor voltage), GND. AO requires an external ADC when interfaced to a board with no analog inputs.
nodes.rationale: Exposing both AO and DO lets the designer trade off continuous concentration readings (needs ADC) against a simple binary threshold event (no ADC), which matters on a Raspberry Pi that has no on-board analog input.
